clue.text: Book anything but easy going?

parts.note: the opposite of easy is hard
'anything but' carries over: the opposite of going onward is going back

explanation.surface: A reader complains that a book is heavy going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anything but' applies to both words: swap easy and going for their opposites. 'Easy going' looks like one phrase meaning relaxed, which hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff boards, as opposed to a paperback edition.

clue.text: Cheerful call from attention-seeker stealing paintings, say

indicators.note: one who steals takes something in and holds it, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: the cry someone makes to get noticed
paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: Someone shouts cheerily while making off with some pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty describes a warm, jovial, cheerful manner.

clue.text: Revolt is contained by band

indicators.note: being contained by something means sitting inside it, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
taken as written

explanation.surface: An uprising is held in check by a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an armed rebellion, as in the Easter Rising, so it is a synonym of revolt.

clue.text: Foundation inspiring family from Indonesia

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one word is drawn inside the other

parts.note: a base is a foundation
a line is a family's line of descent

explanation.surface: A charitable foundation motivates a family from Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Balinese means belonging to Bali, an island province of Indonesia.

clue.text: Name in panic I texted

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the single letter and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone sends a hurried message naming a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite someone is to name them, as when citing a source or a person in a report.

clue.text: Suffering a reverse, those in form prove fallible

indicators.note: a word that suffers a reverse is turned the other way round, read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a form is a school class, and those in it are pupils

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren who suffer a setback show they can make mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is the British word for a school class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is to make a mistake, which shows one is fallible.

clue.text: Pakistani city I see in mythology

indicators.note: one item sits in the other, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: lore is the body of traditional myths and stories
the exclamation of sudden understanding

explanation.surface: Someone spots a Pakistani city in ancient myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province and Pakistan's second-largest city.

clue.text: Dog beginning to bark: further note about that in book

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it, so the note wraps what comes before it

parts.note: a postscript is a further note added to a letter
a stock name for a dog

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of bark

explanation.surface: A book describes a dog that starts to bark, with a footnote about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of wise sayings.

clue.text: Small rooms painters refurbished

indicators.note: something refurbished has been done over and put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Decorators have done up some little rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantries are small rooms or cupboards for storing food.

clue.text: Perfect beau lost in a storm

indicators.note: things caught in a storm are tossed about and thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dashing boyfriend gets lost in bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and perfect both mean complete and total, as in an absolute or perfect stranger.

clue.text: Unseated, seat discussed

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: a throne is a royal seat

explanation.surface: A rider knocked off a horse talks about the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who is thrown has been unseated, pitched off the horse.

clue.text: Minimal amount of funding as 21 strip?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a paltry sum of money
second meaning: Charles Schulz's comic strip about Charlie Brown and Snoopy; 21 is CARTOON

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference turns 21 into CARTOON, giving 'cartoon strip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is slang for a trivial sum of money, and is also the famous Schulz comic strip.

clue.text: Worker stands by figure for rent payer

parts.note: a number
the worker ant

explanation.surface: An employee stands next to a statue for a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands by' means the worker is placed beside the figure, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is someone who pays rent to occupy property.

clue.text: Try to restrain flightless bird, certainly!

indicators.note: to restrain something is to hold it in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case
a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hold back an ostrich-like bird and agrees heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: Hear hear is the cry of strong agreement, as in Parliament, much like saying certainly.

clue.text: I am sent unruly prisoners

indicators.note: unruly means out of order, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warder complains of being sent to deal with rowdy prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmates are the people held in a prison.

clue.text: Silly error entering US state, forgetting capital

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it
capital is a capital letter, the first one, which is forgotten and so dropped

parts.note: the New England state
a sin is a wrongdoing or error

explanation.surface: A blunder is made on arriving in an American state, whose capital is overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a state capital city, but it means the initial capital letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means extremely stupid, literally donkey-like.

clue.text: Clever telegram: don't open it

indicators.note: not opening the word means leaving off its opening letter

parts.note: a cable is a telegram

explanation.surface: A smart telegram arrives with a warning not to open it.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or talented, a synonym of clever.

clue.text: Container of soup somewhere in Greater Manchester has run out

indicators.note: having something out means it has been removed

parts.note: a large town in Greater Manchester
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A soup pan in a northern English town has emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: Greater Manchester is a metropolitan county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot is a large pan in which stock or soup is made.

clue.text: Mixture thus I found in airport

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: a thing found in a place lies inside it

parts.note: London Luton is an airport north of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller reports what they found at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a solution is a liquid mixture with one substance dissolved in another.

clue.text: God poisoned by mistake

indicators.note: a thing done by mistake goes wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deity was accidentally poisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea.

clue.text: Ancient city bringing heart of Paris into play

indicators.note: bringing something into another puts it inside

parts.note: to toy with is to play with

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, the middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of Paris

explanation.surface: An old city's story brings the Trojan prince Paris into a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is apt: he was the Trojan prince who carried off Helen and started the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad, besieged by the Greeks.

clue.text: Box containing old humorous sketch

indicators.note: a thing containing another holds it inside

parts.note: a carton is a box
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A box holds an old comic drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a funny drawing, a humorous sketch.

clue.text: Heading off fight, English prime minister once

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: a battle is a fight
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A former prime minister averts a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the Labour prime minister of Britain from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Attlee led Britain after the Second World War, so he was prime minister once.

clue.text: Might one help you to remember runner?

definitions.text: Might one help you to remember
definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that jogs the memory
second meaning: someone who goes running for exercise

explanation.walkthrough: The first half rests on the phrase 'a memory jogger', a prompt or reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A jogger is both a reminder that prompts recall and a person who runs at an easy pace.

clue.text: Small and pretty, daughter isn't ugly ultimately

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
ain't is the informal form of isn't

indicators.note: ultimately points at the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of ugly

explanation.surface: A girl is described as petite and attractive, not ugly at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty means delicately small and pretty.

clue.text: Beds etc in use, cot needs tidying

indicators.note: something that needs tidying is in a mess and has to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The beds have been slept in and the cot is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' looks like furniture, but it is the usual abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county; etc widens it to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire is one English county, so Beds etc stands for counties in general.

clue.text: Italian city in Milano revered after revolution?

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters are read backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An Italian city is held in high regard in Milan after an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is a city in northern Italy, the setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Don't eat like a sprinter!

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like dietary advice for an athlete; the two halves are separate meanings, a verb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from food, and fast also means speedy, as a sprinter is.

clue.text: Work around border in the proper manner?

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A seamstress stitches round a hem neatly and correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Primly means in a stiffly formal and proper way.

clue.text: Top horse I backed, Jack perhaps on it

parts.note: a jack is an example of a playing card

indicators.note: something backed is moved back, read from its end to its start

parts.note: a nag is a horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter backs the favourite horse with a jockey called Jack riding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On it' places the card first, on top of the reversed pair in a down-style build.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted top that fastens down the front.

clue.text: Cash: singer on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A singer is paid for a radio appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound note, so a sum of cash.

clue.text: Fish: it's angry when provoked

indicators.note: a provoked creature is stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish turns angry when someone disturbs it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a venomous barbed tail.
